prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas. Injury: neck strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1188; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just say I'm the plaintiff in this matter. I'd prefer not to have my full name read into the transcript beyond what's already on file.

Q: That's fine. Let's proceed. Can you describe how the collision happened?

A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Pasadena, Texas, heading toward a shopping center. It was a clear afternoon. A vehicle coming the other way drifted into my lane, and we ended up in a head-on collision. I hit the brakes, but there wasn't much time.

Q: How fast were you traveling at the moment of impact?

A: I'd guess I was going maybe twenty-five miles an hour, nothing fancy. The other car wasn't going much faster. It wasn't a high-speed crash by any means.

Q: Did your airbags deploy?

A: The front airbags did deploy, yes. My head snapped forward and then back, and my neck felt it right away.

Q: Did you seek medical attention that day?

A: Yes. An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They checked me over, took X-rays, and told me I had a neck strain. They gave me a cervical collar and some medication for the pain.

Q: Since that day, what treatment have you received?

A: I went to a physical therapist about two times a week for several weeks. I also did some stretching exercises at home. My primary doctor checked on me a few times. The therapy helped some, but I still get stiffness when I turn my head quickly.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: Mostly it's the small things. I used to run errands and go to the gym most mornings. For a while I couldn't lift anything heavy, and sleeping was harder because I couldn't find a comfortable position. I've had to take breaks when I'm driving, because looking over my shoulder to change lanes can be uncomfortable.

Q: Have you missed any work?

A: I missed a few days right after the accident, and I was on light duty for a short period. I've been back to my normal schedule for a while now.

Q: Do you have any pain today?

A: Some days are better than others. On bad days I get a dull ache at the base of my neck that goes up into my head. I manage it with over-the-counter medication and heat packs.
